Presentation 
Sneha Gavankar 
Good day and welcome to Tata Motors Limited Q2 FY27 Earnings Call. I have with me today Mr. Girish 
Wagh, Managing Director and CEO; Mr. GV Ramanan, CFO and the Investor Relations team. Today we'll 
walk you through the results presentation followed by Q&A. As a reminder, all participants will be in listen-
only mode and we will be taking questions by the Teams platform. The same is already open to you for 
submitting questions. You are requested to mention your name and the name of your organization while 
submitting the questions. With that, I now hand over to Mr. GV Ramanan. Over to you.  
 
GV Ramanan 
Thank you, Sneha. Good evening and welcome to Tata Motors Q2 FY27 Earnings Call. Thank you for joining 
us today. I'll be taking you through our financial performance for the quarter and the half-year ended 
September 30, 2026.  
 
Safe harbour statement. This is the regular statement that we have given, and like last quarter, our primary 
numbers represent the standalone financials, which include the joint operations with Tata Cummins. 
Consolidated results follow later in the deck. There is no change in the reporting parameters versus this 
quarter. Freight Tiger continues to be consolidated as a subsidiary, as it was in Q1. With that, let me take 
you through the highlights of the call.  
On products, at Prawaas 5.0 we unveiled our next-generation passenger mobility solution, including the 
launch of new Ultra Prime and Starbus Prime range. We also showcased our next-gen aggregates portfolio 
at Bauma CONEXPO India 2026. We were crowned the Best Truck of the Year at the Logistics and Transport 
Award 2026 in the UAE, a recognition that comes alongside a very strong quarter of export, which I will 
cover under the volume section. Signed MoU with Drivn to offer innovative leasing and financing solutions 
for our electric commercial vehicles, easing the total cost of ownership conversation for fleet customers. 
We collaborated with Petronas to pilot a scalable used-oil recycling model, extending the circular economy 
work we began with HPCL last quarter. During the quarter, we also partnered with Welspun Renewable 
Energy to develop a 86-megawatt wind-solar hybrid project.  
A quick update on IVECO transaction, which has progressed in line with the timeline we shared last quarter. 
We obtained all required regulatory clearances, completing the condition to launch the offer. 
Consequently, the acceptance period opened on 7 September 2026 and will close on 26 October 2026. On 
9 October, we increased the offer price from EUR14.10 to EUR14.40 per share in consideration of the slight

October 23, 2026

delay in completing the offer relative to the original timeline. This was a goodwill gesture from the 
company, and EUR14.40 has also been declared as a best and final offer. On 16 October, IVECO EGM 
approved all offer-related resolutions. As of 22 October, approximately 35% of shares have been tendered. 
As typically seen in the tender offer process, a significant portion of shares tend to be tendered towards 
the very end of the acceptance period, particularly in the final 24 to 48 hours. We therefore remain 
confident of a successful completion of the open offer. Subject to the offer conditions being met, 
settlement is expected on 30 October 2026, when Tata Motors will pay the offer price for the shares 
tendered. We will come back to you with an update on IVECO once the offer is settled. 
Q2 wholesales were at 1,35,100 units, up 42% year-on-year and up 24% sequentially. Growth was once 
again broad-based, with every segment in double digits. HCV was up 41%, ILMCV was up 24%, small 
commercial cargo and pickup was up 27%, CV passenger up 31%, and international business was up 177%, 
close to 2.6 times over last year. The step up in international business that you see is driven by the 
Indonesian order, where deliveries ramped up sharply during the quarter on top of the steady export 
trajectory we built through FY26. 
For the half year, wholesales were at 2,43,800 units, up 35%. HCV up 32%, ILMCV up 20%, small 
commercial pickup, again a double-digit growth of 30%, and CV passenger was up 26%, and the 
international business was up 114%.  
The next few slides cover the standalone business, including the joint operations with Tata Cummins. 
 
The Financial Highlight. This slide summarizes the standalone financials, including the joint operations with 
Cummins. Volume momentum translated into 42% revenue growth. Revenue for Q2 was ₹23,900 crores. 
EBITDA was about ₹2,800 crores, up 31% at a margin of 11.7%. While EBITDA margin was down 90 basis 
points YoY, it held flat sequentially despite a commodity headwind intensifying further during the quarter. 
I will take you through the margin walk later. 
EBIT margin was at 9.7%, down 50 basis points YoY. EBIT at ₹2,300 crores. The profit before tax, before 
exceptional items, was at ₹2,700 crores, up 51%. So, an absolute profit growth has again outpaced volume 
growth. Free cash flow was at ₹4,600 crores against ₹2,200 crores in Q2 last year, an improvement of 
₹2,400 crore, which I'll walk you through shortly. With that, the net cash stood at ₹11,300 crores as at 
September 30 against ₹7,500 crores at March and ₹7,100 crores at June end, and this is after the dividend 
payout in Q1. 
The Auto ROCE was 65% on a trailing 12-month basis against 68% at the end of Q1, a moderation largely 
reflecting the lower margins over the last 12 months. Investment spends was ₹600 crore for the quarter 
against ₹700 crore in Q2 last year, and this is in line with the plan. 
Coming to the Q2 EBIT walk. This is the walk from PBT before exceptional items of ₹1,757 crores in Q2 
FY26 to ₹2,660 crores in Q2 FY27, with the EBIT margins bridge shown underneath. Volume and mix 
contributed to around ₹1,159 crore, with an improved net realization of further ₹1,017 crores. Together, 
these added 230 basis points to EBIT margin. Variable cost, with the principal headwinds at ₹1,416 crore, 
590 basis point impact. This is the commodity inflation which was flowing into the material cost. Other 
cost contributed positively at 280 bps. Even though they were higher in absolute terms by ₹214 crores,

depreciation, product development were favourable by ₹13 crores, employee cost was higher by ₹88 
crores, and other expenses by ₹139 crores. This is operating leverage on a 42% larger revenue base. FX 
and other items added 30 basis points, or ₹350 crores. Other income of ₹118 crore, lower finance cost of 
₹134 crores, and a Forex gain of ₹24 crores, and ₹80 crores of other items, including PLI incentive. Net of 
all this, EBIT margin moved from 10.2% to 9.7%. To summarize, a 590 bps commodity headwind has been 
almost entirely offset by operating leverage, cost efficiency, and improved realization. 
Coming to the free cash flow for the quarter, FCF was at ₹4,600 crores against ₹2,210 crores in Q2 FY26 
and ₹5,721 crores for the half year. If we look at the Q2 walk, PBT before exceptional items stood at ₹2,660 
crores and non-cash items was around ₹389 crores. Tax was ₹762 crores against ₹337 crores in Q2 last 
year. And as I said, at the full-year results, tax is now a recurring item for us, and it will scale with profit. 
That gives us a cash profit after tax of ₹2,287 crores for Q2, which is up 26% YoY. Capex was ₹483 crores, 
broadly in line with last year and with plan. Working capital released ₹2,679 crore in this quarter. With 
that, payable and acceptances released around ₹4,786 crore on the back of a strong volume ramp-up, 
while inventories absorbed around ₹1,717 crore and receivable around ₹622 crore, both of which reflect 
the build for the Indonesia order and the higher run rate going into the festive season. I would want to 
mention here that part of this working capital release is timing-related and will partially reverse as 
payables normalize as we move forward.  
Investment spending. Total Investment spending in Q2 was ₹597 crores against ₹686 crores in Q2 FY26, 
taking the half-year to around ₹1,112 crore. Research and development in Q2 was ₹339 crores, ₹209 crore 
capitalized and ₹130 crore expensed. For H1, R&D was ₹616 crores. Capital and other investments were 
₹258 crores in Q2 and ₹496 crore for the half year. At approximately 2.5% of revenue, this remains 
comfortably within our guided range of 2% to 4%, and we continue to invest steadily in line with plan. 
Coming to consolidated financials. The consolidated revenue for Q2 was ₹25,300 crores, up 36% YoY. 
EBITDA was ₹2,800 crores, up 31% at a margin of 10.9%, down 40 bps. EBIT margin was 8.9%, up to 20 
basis points. So, at the consolidated level, we have actually expanded EBIT margin supported by operating 
leverage and share of profits from JVs and associates. Profit before tax before exceptional items was ₹1,800 
crores against a loss of ₹550 crore in Q2 FY26. The comparison is distorted by the mark-to-market on our 
investment in Tata Capital. Excluding the mark-to-market, underlying PBT grew strongly and in line with 
the standalone trend. 
Consolidated free cash flow was ₹3,000 crores against ₹2,000 crores in Q2 FY26. Net cash stood at ₹15,900 
crores as at September 30 against ₹13,700 crores at March end, which includes Tata Motors Finance 
Holding gross debt net of the market value of its investment in Tata Capital. This puts us at a very strong 
liquidity position going forward in H2 FY27. 
 
With that, let me hand this over to Girish to take you through the business update. Over to you, Girish. 
Girish Wagh 
Thank You, Ramanan. Let me begin with the market share story. So overall, our H1 VAHAN market share 
stands at 36.2%, which is 110 basis points higher than the FY26 level, reflecting an improvement in overall 
market position on a YoY basis. In Heavy Commercial Vehicles, we continue to maintain a strong leadership

position in H1 market share at 55.7%, improving by 50 basis points over FY26. In ILMCV, H1 market share 
stands at 36.3%, and a good part of this also has been due to supply chain constraints in this particular 
segment. Then coming to SCV pickups, the trajectory has been positive, with H1 market share improving 
to 27.6%. So, it is an increase of 130 basis points over FY26. CV Passenger registered H1 market share of 
41.1%, up 500 basis points over FY26, reflecting a strong momentum across the segment. Overall, we have 
gained market share, and our focus in H2 will be to improve on these gains. 
Moving on. Regarding fleet utilization, this is our internal data using the Fleet Edge, and fleet utilization 
remained broadly stable to improving gradually during the quarter, indicating sustained operating intensity 
across the fleet. The freight rates also strengthened during Q2, providing support to transporter 
economics. From our discussions with the transporters, the profitability had seen some pressure at the 
beginning of the quarter post the diesel price increase, but gradually through the quarter it has started to 
recover. So, looking at all these together, the utilization, freight rates, and the recovery in transporter 
profitability indicate a relatively stable operating environment for the fleet operators. 
Let me now talk about the industry. Q2 saw healthy momentum in the Commercial Vehicle industry with 
industry offtake growing 28.4% year-on-year while our volumes grew at 30.5%. Freight activity remained 
robust through the quarter, recovering from the monsoon-led slowdown in July, supported by stronger 
infrastructure execution, improved mining output, festive inventory stocking, and automotive dispatches. 
The broader operating indicators remain supportive, with healthy E-way bill generation reflecting 
increased goods movement and consumption demand, and the fleet utilization improved progressively 
through the quarter. 
As we enter H2, the underlying demand environment still remains healthy, supported by, of course, at an 
overall level, the GDP growth, but therefore that leading to increased freight availability, stable fleet 
utilization, infrastructure activity, and consumption-led movement. Beyond the near term, we remain 
positive on the structural outlook of the CV industry, which is supported by the economic growth and 
therefore increasing road freight, infrastructure development, and the replacement demand. 
Talking of the specific businesses. So, the key takeaway from Q2 is that the growth momentum was broad-
based across the portfolio, with healthy performance across trucks, the passenger carriers, and small 
commercial vehicles, alongside strong progress in our international business as also the downstream 
businesses. International business was a strong growth contributor during the quarter, with volumes 
growing 177% year-on-year, mainly supported by the Indonesia order as well as the momentum across 
our other international segment. 
In Parts & Services, we continued the healthy trajectory, sustaining growth in the aftermarket business, 
improving spare parts penetration, and strengthening the customer uptime proposition. Our digital 
business is also progressing well with FleetEdge renewal rates improving, thereby strengthening the 
recurring digital revenue opportunity. The e-bus operations in Smart City also continue to scale while 
maintaining more than 95% fleet uptime across the major operating fleets, demonstrating the progress 
we are making in building this business. 
Coming to sustainability, the EV momentum built further and remained strong in Q2 with overall EV 
volumes growing 143% year-on-year. Within this, the small commercial vehicle EV retails crossed 4,400

units in Q2, registering a 2.9 times year-on-year growth, and this was also constrained by the supply chain 
and availability of some of the imported aggregates. Otherwise, it could have been more. 
EV Trucks continue to see improving customer traction and adoption. In e-buses, as I mentioned in Smart 
City, the operations continue to do well with more than 95% uptime, and we have now covered more than 
64 crore green kilometres since inception. So overall, the quarter saw broad-based momentum across the 
core vehicle businesses, international business, downstream businesses, and EVs, with the focus remaining 
on disciplined execution and profitable growth. 
Now looking ahead in Q3 and maybe beyond, our priority is to leverage the healthy demand momentum 
while balancing pricing, cost efficiency, and supply readiness to drive profitable growth. In trucks, we will 
capitalize on healthy demand through portfolio actions focused on improving customer productivity, 
payload, and the total cost of ownership. 
In CV Passenger, we will capture opportunities across institutional and passenger mobility, including state 
transport, school and staff transportation, while progressively scaling electric buses. In SCV pickups, we 
will build on the portfolio enhancement and increasing EV adoption supported by resilient last-mile and 
e-commerce demand. In Parts & Services, the priority is to build a larger and more resilient aftermarket 
business by improving customer uptime offerings and expanding service reach. 
In international business, we will continue to diversify and scale across geographies while maintaining 
disciplined execution across channels, products, and markets while navigating geopolitical volatility. On 
IVECO, consolidation will begin next quarter, with immediate priority being to ensure a seamless transition. 
Overall, the Q3 agenda is about sustaining growth momentum while maintaining discipline on profitability, 
execution, and readiness for the next phase of the business. 
 
Thank you. 
 
Questions And Answers 
 
Sneha Gavankar 
Yeah. So, we'll get into Q&A now, but a couple of questions which are common across which maybe I'll 
start off with that. So, one question is how much more of commodity pressures expected in the next 
quarter. And if you could talk about the price hikes that we've taken so far. 
 
Girish Wagh 
Yes. So, commodity inflation actually continues to be a major headwind. And beyond that, of course, we 
keep monitoring the oil prices, but commodity inflation has already been played out over Q1, Q2, and 
even in Q3, we see that happening again. And on a YoY basis, the commodity cost impact has been almost 
540 bps. On a quarter-on-quarter basis, from Q1 to Q2, it has been 200 bps. We expect a further 
commodity cost increase in Q3 in the range of around maybe 150 to 200 bps, depending upon where some 
of the major commodities do settle. 
Within that, I would say steel and rubber will continue to be the largest driver. Steel, in fact, all of you 
know, that is already at a 52-week high with almost 40% growth on a YoY basis. Rubber, this remains the

input we expect to stay elevated for some time. Supply is tight and crude-linked synthetic rubber costs are 
also increasing. So, we are watching it closely and factoring it in our planning. 
On pricing, as you are aware, we have taken already four pricing actions during the year, around 1% in 
January, around 2% in April, 2.5% in July, and then from 1 October, we have taken another 1% to 2% 
increase depending upon the segment. There has been a significant amount of price increase that has 
been taken through the year. It certainly doesn't cover the commodity increases that we have seen. But 
as we have been saying, I think our first line of action has always been to see what we can do on the cost 
side, which is what we have been doing, and we are trying to balance this demand momentum with very 
measured pricing actions. I think that's where we are from an overall basis. 
If I may also upfront address the demand question, because quite a few of them have asked about demand. 
I think we are now into maybe three weeks of October, and the demand momentum continues. But as we 
have been saying, the YoY growth rates will taper now. Because post-GST rate rationalization, the demand 
had picked up in last year third quarter. Last year, third quarter saw 21.5% growth on a YoY basis. Now, we 
expect that even this Q3, it appears that we will see a very high single-digit or beginning of double-digit 
kind of growth. For the overall quarter, maximum growth within this is likely to be in intermediate light to 
medium commercial vehicles, certainly double-digit. CV passenger also will see a double-digit growth, but 
heavy commercial vehicles and small commercial vehicles are likely to now see a single-digit growth, but 
even that on the higher single-digit side. So, I think that's what we see as the likely demand growth. 
However, I must say that we have to closely monitor both the demand headwinds as well as tailwinds. I 
think on the headwinds, as I said in the beginning, diesel prices will continue to be a very important 
monitorable, as also the interest rates. I think a 25-basis point hike has already been taken. This, of course, 
will not dent the demand much, but it remains an important monitorable. So sorry, a longish answer, but 
it probably addresses some of the underlying questions.

or there may be a decline in LCV exports after FY28? 
Girish Wagh 
As we have said in the last analyst call also, Indonesia order to a large extent will be delivered over two 
years, so this financial year and the next financial year. And currently, we are supplying at the rate of 
anywhere between 4,500 to 5,000 a month. The total order is almost of 70,000. We are, of course, using 
this opportunity to see how we can strengthen our presence in this market because 70,000 is a significant 
opportunity.  
So, a lot of actions are being taken on retail financing tie-ups, distribution, and service setups. And like you 
have asked, yes, we will certainly leverage this opportunity to bring in some of the other segments. 
What I would also like to mention is the international business, from Q1 to Q2, the non-Indonesia business 
has also seen healthy growth, and this has been because some of the markets, especially Sub-Saharan 
Africa, Nepal, and Sri Lanka, I think these stabilized post the immediate impact of the geopolitical issues,
